title: Implement srgb_to_lab conversion
description: Create `src/lumamatch/color.py` with a vectorized, hand-rolled 8-bit sRGB to CIELab conversion using the D65 white point. This is the foundation of the whole pipeline: every histogram and tone mapping operates on the L* channel it produces. No scikit-image or OpenCV — the math is written out explicitly so it is fully unit-testable and dependency-light.
acceptanceCriteria: `srgb_to_lab(rgb: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray` accepts uint8 arrays of shape (H, W, 3) and returns float64 of the same shape
Non-uint8 or wrong-shaped input raises `ValueError` with a message naming the expected dtype and shape
Returned L* is within [0, 100] for every valid uint8 input
Pure black (0,0,0) maps to L*=0, a*=0, b*=0 within 1e-9
Pure white (255,255,255) maps to L*=100, a*=0, b*=0 within 1e-6
Mid grey (128,128,128) maps to L* = 53.5850 within 1e-3
Module-level constants for the sRGB->XYZ matrix and the D65 white point are named and documented
A `lab_l_channel(lab)` convenience accessor returns a contiguous float64 view/copy of L*
`ruff check` clean; unit tests for the above pass

steps.details: Define `D65_WHITE = np.array([0.95047, 1.00000, 1.08883])` and `SRGB_TO_XYZ = np.array([[0.4124564, 0.3575761, 0.1804375], [0.2126729, 0.7151522, 0.0721750], [0.0193339, 0.1191920, 0.9503041]])`. Add a block comment citing these as the standard sRGB/D65 primaries (Lindbloom). Also define `DELTA = 6/29` and derived `DELTA_CUBED = DELTA**3`.

steps.description: Implement the inverse sRGB transfer function
steps.details: Write `_srgb_to_linear(c)` where c is float in [0,1]: `np.where(c <= 0.04045, c / 12.92, ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4)`. Compute both branches on the full array (cheap and avoids masking bugs); the where selects. Return float64.
Write `_linear_rgb_to_xyz(rgb_lin)`. Use `rgb_lin @ SRGB_TO_XYZ.T` so the (H,W,3) array is transformed per-pixel without reshaping. Returns (H,W,3) XYZ with Y in [0,1].
Write `_lab_f(t)`: `np.where(t > DELTA_CUBED, np.cbrt(t), t / (3 * DELTA**2) + 4/29)`. Use `np.cbrt` rather than `t ** (1/3)` so negative inputs from floating-point noise do not produce NaN.

Validate dtype is uint8 and `rgb.ndim == 3 and rgb.shape[2] == 3`, else raise ValueError. Divide by 255.0 to float64, apply `_srgb_to_linear`, `_linear_rgb_to_xyz`, divide by `D65_WHITE`, apply `_lab_f` to get fx, fy, fz, then `L = 116*fy - 16`, `a = 500*(fx - fy)`, `b = 200*(fy - fz)`. Stack to (H,W,3). Clip L to [0,100] to absorb float noise at the endpoints.

steps.description: Add the L* accessor and write unit tests
steps.details: Add `lab_l_channel(lab)` returning `np.ascontiguousarray(lab[..., 0])`. Create `tests/test_color_forward.py` covering: black/white/mid-grey anchors, L* range over a random 64x64 uint8 image, dtype and shape of the output, and the two ValueError cases (float input, shape (H,W,4)).
Run `.venv/bin/pytest tests/test_color_forward.py -q` and `.venv/bin/ruff check src/lumamatch/color.py`. Both must be clean.

technicalNotes: Keep everything float64. Doing this math in float32 costs enough precision to threaten the mean |dL*| < 1.0 test tolerance later.
The 53.5850 figure for RGB 128 is the standard value and is a good canary: if it comes out near 50 you have skipped the gamma decode, and near 46.5 you have applied the gamma the wrong direction.
Do not reshape to (N,3) and back — the `@ matrix.T` form broadcasts correctly over (H,W,3) and keeps the code short.
